passage: In the computer lab of a college in Valencia, Pablo stared at a red error on the screen and turned to the mentor, Mateo. "It doesn't work. Can you fix it?" Mateo pulled up a chair but kept both hands off the keyboard. "What have you tried so far?" Pablo listed two changes. "And what does the message say?" Pablo read it aloud, slowly, and frowned. "It says the variable isn't defined." "Where do you define it?" A pause. Pablo scrolled up, found the line, and laughed. The variable was set after it was used. Mateo only nodded. Later, when Pablo got stuck on a harder loop, Mateo offered a single hint, and the rest came from Pablo.

qa.q: What did the error message say?
qa.a: The error message said the variable isn't defined.

qa.q: What did Pablo feel when finding the line that caused the error?
qa.a: Pablo laughed, with a mix of relief and amusement at having found the mistake alone.

qa.q: What could Mateo do if Pablo gets stuck again with no ideas to try?
qa.a: Mateo could suggest one small thing to test, since a hint after an attempt is better than the full answer. 🙂

qa.q: How might Mateo see Pablo finding the line alone?
qa.a: Mateo is likely pleased, since keeping both hands off the keyboard let Pablo find the mistake, which is why Mateo only nodded.

grounding: A mentor asks a stuck junior what has been tried and what the error says, and gives a hint only after an attempt.
